title: STREAM-SCOPE ABAC IS NEVER EVALUATED. The handler exists, is registered in DI, and is unit-tested - and NO POLICY CARRIES THE REQUIREMENT, so ASP.NET never invokes it. It fails OPEN. Found 2026-08-13 while scoping Tranche B's AC-010 fixture. THE MEASUREMENT, and it was three lines: AuthorizationRegistration.cs:64 did `services.AddScoped<IAuthorizationHandler, StreamScopeHandler>()`; AuthorizationRegistration.cs:69 built EVERY policy as `options.AddPolicy(policy, p => p.AddRequirements(new CapabilityRequirement(policy, allow, owner)))` - CapabilityRequirement and nothing else; and a grep for StreamScopeRequirement across src and tests returned only its own definition, a comment in ResourceAuthorizer, Topic.cs implementing the marker interface, and AbacHandlerTests. ResourceAuthorizer evaluates `AuthorizeAsync(user, resource, POLICY)`, so a requirement absent from every policy is never reached. WHY THIS WAS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT ANYONE WOULD SPOT: a reviewer asking 'is stream scope implemented?' found a handler, a DI registration, an aggregate implementing IStreamScopedResource, and four passing unit tests exercising in-scope, out-of-scope, no-subject and committee-wide-bypass. All four answers were yes. The only thing missing was the wiring that would make any of it run, and nothing in the codebase asserted that. THE CONSEQUENCE: permission-role-matrix E.1 says stream-bounded roles may only write against resources in their own streams; they could write against ANY topic, because nothing checked. It FAILED OPEN, which is the opposite of the fail-closed behaviour first assumed and is why no 403 had ever been reported. Blast radius was bounded by the trust model - a single committee of <=20 authenticated insiders - so this was a specified control that was absent, not an exposure to outsiders. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #269 (squash 1f0cbcd), ADR-0043 step 7, as the LAST step of an eight-step slice whose ORDER was load-bearing: seed the taxonomy -> topic picker -> assignment UI -> invite requires a stream -> backfill everyone -> fix the fail-open paths -> WIRE IT. Wiring it earlier would have taken the system from fails-open straight to refuses-everything, which is why the ADR forbade it. AuthorizationRegistration.StreamScoped now names the policies carrying the requirement and holds exactly ONE - Policies.TopicEdit, the only policy both stream-bounded per E.1 and evaluated with a resource. The wildcard is read from Stream.IsWildcard in the same query that returns the codes (DW-026), never by matching the code, so the members the step-5 backfill protected are unrestricted rather than refused. ⚠ THE SECOND, COMPOUNDING FACT IN THIS ROW WAS ALSO FIXED, and first: 'NO STREAM CAN EVER BE CREATED' - Stream.Create had no caller and nothing seeded the table. Step 1 seeded the taxonomy by migration. ⚠ AND THE THIRD MISMATCH THIS ROW FLAGGED - free-text topic streams versus code-shaped Stream.Code - was closed by step 2's picker and the shared MustBeSeededStreams validator. EVIDENCE: an owner assigned to 'government' is refused prepare on a 'core' topic and the identical request succeeds once they hold 'core'; mutation-checked by removing TopicEdit from StreamScoped, which restores the 204 this row describes. ⚠ AC-010's LIVE E2E LEG IS STEP 8 AND IS NOT DONE - the control now runs, but the acceptance criterion is not yet evidenced through the browser.

title: Topic.SetScope HAS NO CALLER - the Secretary cannot elevate a topic to Platform or OrgWide, so those two enum values can never occur. FOURTH instance this session of an aggregate capability with no way to reach it. Found 2026-08-13 while checking the operator's (CORRECT) recollection that an 'all streams' concept already existed on the topic side. IT DOES: TopicScope { SingleStream = 1, MultiStream = 2, Platform = 3, OrgWide = 4 }, whose own comment reads 'Drives the required reviewer/voter set and notification audience. Derived from affected-stream count at submission (1 -> SingleStream, >=2 -> MultiStream); THE SECRETARY MAY ELEVATE TO PLATFORM/ORGWIDE DURING TRIAGE.' Topic.cs:233 provides `public void SetScope(TopicScope scope)`, and Topic.cs:228 confirms scope stays editable post-Accept until Decided. THE MEASUREMENT: SetScope has NO caller anywhere. UpdateTopicCommand carries TopicId, Title, Description, Justification, Urgency, Streams, Systems and Tags - and NO Scope. A grep for scope across TopicEndpoints.cs returns nothing at all. So DeriveScope() is the only writer and can only ever produce SingleStream or MultiStream; Platform and OrgWide are unreachable enum values. CONSEQUENCE: the taxonomy's own escalation path does not exist. A platform-wide architecture decision is recorded as MultiStream because it happened to list two streams, and the reviewer/voter set and notification audience that TopicScope is documented to drive are computed from stream COUNT alone, with no way for a human to correct them. ⚠ THE PATTERN IS THE REAL FINDING, AND THIS IS ITS FOURTH INSTANCE IN ONE SESSION: Topic.Reopen (aggregate method, no endpoint - which is why AC-009's positive clause is unreachable), Stream.Create (factory, no caller - DEF-057), StreamScopeRequirement (handler registered in DI, in no policy - DEF-057), and now Topic.SetScope. Each looks implemented from every angle a reviewer checks: the domain method exists, it is correct, and in two cases it is unit-tested. What is missing every time is the WIRING, and NOTHING IN THE BUILD ASSERTS WIRING. A guard that fails when a public aggregate method has no production caller would have caught all four. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #267 (squash ca3bf05), ADR-0043 step 6. UpdateTopicCommand now carries an OPTIONAL TopicScope, bound from UpdateTopicBody, and UpdateTopicHandler is SetScope's caller. ⚠ THE GATE IS SEPARATE FROM THE EDIT AND APPLIES AT EVERY STATUS, which is the part that needed care rather than typing: elevating scope WIDENS write access to every stream-bounded member (ADR-0043 clause 5), and the pre-Accept branch deliberately lets a submitter edit their own topic with NO ABAC check at all - so folding scope into that branch would have let the submitter of any topic hand the whole committee write access to it. A changed scope therefore carries Policies.TopicTriage wherever it happens, and is audited on its own verb (Topics.TopicScopeChanged) because an escalation buried inside a generic 'topic updated' event cannot answer 'who widened access to this topic'. Omitting Scope means 'leave it alone' and costs no authorization. DeriveScope already preserved an elevated scope, which is why elevation was safe to add; that guard is now covered by a test of its own. THE UI HALF the row asked for is the AC-034 edit flow, built in the same PR by DEC-045/SC-010 - PUT /api/topics/{id} had had NO SPA caller at all.

title: STREAM SCOPE HAD A SECOND FAIL-OPEN PATH, ON THE RESOURCE SIDE, AND IT WAS REACHABLE OVER HTTP: a topic could be edited to have ZERO streams, and StreamScopeHandler treated an empty resource-stream set as SUCCEED. Found 2026-08-13 while reading StreamScopeRequirement.cs to scope ADR-0042 step 7. ⚠ NOT THE SAME HOLE AS DEF-057. DEF-057 is 'the requirement is in no policy, so the handler never runs'. THIS row is 'even once the handler DOES run, one reachable state makes it grant universally'. THE MEASUREMENT, traced end to end: (1) StreamScopeRequirement.cs:37-41 read `if (resource.AffectedStreams.Count == 0) { context.Succeed(requirement); return; }` - an unconditional grant. (2) Topic.cs:104 requires >=1 stream to SUBMIT - the guard everyone stops reading at, and it runs once. (3) Topic.cs:229 AssignStreams called ReplaceStrings, which clears then adds nothing on an empty input; its ONLY guard was EnsureMutable(). (4) UpdateTopicValidator declared rules for TopicId and Urgency ONLY - no rule on Streams, unlike SubmitTopicValidator's NotEmpty. (5) UpdateTopicHandler called topic.AssignStreams(request.Streams) unconditionally. (6) TopicEndpoints.cs:101 maps PUT /api/topics/{id} passing the list straight through. SO: PUT with "streams": [] left a live, non-Decided topic with AffectedStreams.Count == 0, and every stream-bounded member then passed stream scope on it. THE ASYMMETRY WAS THE ROOT CAUSE AND IS THE GENERALIZABLE PART: submit enforced the invariant, update did not, and the aggregate did not enforce it either - so an invariant asserted at one entry point was silently absent at the other. ⚠ THE WIDER CONSEQUENCE, independent of topics: IStreamScopedResource is a SHARED contract, so any future implementer (Actions, Risks, ADRs) would have inherited this universal grant for free, without its author ever seeing the line. ✅ RESOLVED BY DEC-043 - the operator chose BOTH halves - AND FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #267 (squash ca3bf05), ADR-0043 step 6. HALF ONE: Topic.AssignStreams now throws when a non-Draft topic would be left with no streams, plus NotEmpty on UpdateTopicCommand.Streams. ⚠ The guard is in the SHARED AGGREGATE METHOD, not the one validator - AssignStreams has other callers, and patching the path this row named would have left every sibling caller able to empty a topic; the validator exists as well so the refusal reaches the caller as a 400 naming the field rather than a 409 from a domain exception. A DRAFT MAY STILL HOLD NONE, deliberately: the submission form autosaves as the user types, so a draft is incomplete by design and Submit (AC-030) is the gate it must pass. HALF TWO: IStreamScopedResource gained the primitive bool AffectsAllStreams that ADR-0043 clause (6) mandates, which Topic computes from its own TopicScope (Platform/OrgWide) - the handler now requires a resource to DECLARE itself unscoped instead of inferring it from an empty list, so an empty set denies and no future implementer inherits a universal grant silently. Both halves mutation-checked: removing the aggregate guard fails A_live_topic_cannot_be_emptied_of_streams, weakening the validator fails Update_rejects_an_empty_stream_list, and restoring the empty-list inference fails both the denies-empty and declares-all-streams tests.

title: GUEST PRESENTERS WOULD BE LOCKED OUT BY ADR-0042 STEP 7, AND THE STEP-5 BACKFILL CANNOT SAVE THEM - they are created per-meeting, AFTER any one-time backfill runs. Found 2026-08-13 while scoping step 4 (the invite's required stream field), by asking which OTHER paths create members. THE MEASUREMENT, three facts that only bite together: (1) StreamScopeRequirement.cs:16-17 defined CommitteeWide = { Chairman, Secretary, Auditor, Administrator }. GUEST WAS NOT IN IT, and since the handler bypassed ONLY that list, a Guest would be treated as stream-bounded and must intersect the resource's streams to write. (2) AuthorizationRegistration.cs:48 gives Guest exactly one write capability - Policies.DiagramAttach, as an allow-if-owner role (FR-159 guest presenters attach diagrams to the topic they present). (3) A guest presenter is NOT created by InviteUserCommand. GuestProvisioner.cs:39 calls the same MemberInvitation.InviteAsync, but NEITHER path assigns a stream, and step 4 adds the required stream field to the ADMIN INVITE ONLY. ⚠ WHY THE BACKFILL DOES NOT COVER IT: DEC-044's backfill is a ONE-TIME EF data migration over the members that exist when it runs, while a guest is provisioned when a meeting invites them - always LATER. title: core-loop.spec.ts PUBLISHED THE AGENDA WITHOUT WAITING FOR THE PRESENTER ASSIGNMENT TO LAND, so it intermittently 409'd in CI - a genuine race in the SPEC, not a product defect. Observed 2026-08-13 on PR #264: the SAME branch content passed e2e on its first run (7m58s) and failed on the second, with only a frontend TEST FILE committed in between - a file that cannot touch agenda publishing. That contrast is what makes it flakiness rather than a regression, and it is the cheapest evidence available: two runs of the same code, opposite outcomes. THE MECHANISM, traced rather than guessed: the spec selects a presenter by clicking a dropdown option, which fires an async POST against the agenda item, then immediately clicks 'Publish & notify' and waits only for the PUBLISH response - nothing waits for the presenter POST. The spec's OWN comment states the invariant it is racing: 'Every agenda item needs a presenter before the agenda can be published (domain invariant).' If the POST has not landed, the agenda still holds an item with no presenter, the aggregate refuses, and GlobalExceptionHandler.cs:27 maps InvalidOperationException to 409 Conflict - exactly the observed Received: 409 against Expected: 200. ⚠ IT IS NOT THE OPTIMISTIC-CONCURRENCY 409: GlobalExceptionHandler maps TWO exceptions to 409 - DbUpdateConcurrencyException (a stale RowVersion) and InvalidOperationException (a refused state transition). The publish call sends no client-side RowVersion at all (meetings.ts:310 POSTs with no body), so the concurrency reading is unavailable and the domain-refusal reading is the only one left. A reader who stopped at '409 means stale write' would chase ADR-0018 and find nothing. ⚠ IT IS ALSO NOT THE STALE-DATABASE CLASS: CI REBUILDS THE DATABASE EVERY RUN and is blind to that class by construction, so a CI-only intermittent failure cannot be it. This is a within-run ordering race, which CI's load makes MORE likely rather than less. ⚠ THE UI CANNOT HELP: AgendaBuilder.tsx:216 enables Publish on items.length alone, so Playwright's auto-wait-for-enabled gives no protection. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #271 (squash b12f7e7) under DEC-046: the spec awaits the presenter POST before publishing, wrapping the option click in a waitForResponse exactly as the publish click already does. NOT by retrying publish and NOT by accepting 409 - either would hide a real refusal if the invariant ever broke for a genuine reason. ⚠ THE FIX BRANCH HAD BEEN RECORDED AS NEVER TYPE-CHECKED OR RUN (the headless session that wrote it had tsc and e2e blocked), so it was VERIFIED before merging rather than trusted: rebased onto main, tsc clean, the spec still registers its test, and MeetingsEndpoints.cs:97 returns Results.Ok - confirming the new expect(presRes.status()).toBe(200) is correct, which was the single line most likely to be wrong in an unrun fix. THE FLAKE WAS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the e2e run on PR #269 reported '66 passed + 1 flaky', and reconciling that count against PR #270's 69 is what confirmed both the flake and that two new tests had actually run.

THE MEASUREMENT, four facts: (1) A DATA MIGRATION CAN ONLY TOUCH ROWS THAT EXIST WHEN IT RUNS. (2) Acmp.Api.Tests uses the InMemory provider and NEVER RUNS MIGRATIONS. (3) Acmp.Integration.Tests DOES migrate, but against an EMPTY database, so the backfill is a no-op. (4) The e2e stack migrates a FRESH database, then seeds users into KEYCLOAK; their ACMP member rows are created later by JIT provisioning (ADR-0004), and ProvisionCurrentUser ASSIGNS NO STREAMS. So in every fresh environment the backfill is inert and every e2e fixture user ends up stream-bounded with zero streams. ⚠ THE PRODUCTION SIDE IS UNAFFECTED AND THE DECISION WAS RIGHT; only my note about its blast radius was inverted. ✅ THIS ROW'S OWN BLAST-RADIUS PREDICTION WAS THEN ALSO WRONG, AND DEF-068 MEASURED WHY. It predicted the whole core loop would go red at step 7. It did not: EVERY e2e caller of a TopicEdit-gated route is a SECRETARY, who is not stream-bounded, and TopicEdit is the only stream-scoped policy evaluated with a resource. This row reasoned from ROLES; the answer was in CALL SITES. CI settled it - PR #269 wired the requirement and the e2e job passed. ✅ THE SUBSTANCE IS DISCHARGED, 2026-08-14. The generalisable half - 'a migration's blast radius is ROWS EXISTING AT MIGRATION TIME, and in any environment built fresh that set is EMPTY' - remains true and is exactly what led to DEF-065 (production's row set is far smaller than its account set) and to DEF-071 (a reconciliation run AFTER boot cannot be reached by a backfill that ran AT boot). title: I SHIPPED BROKEN ARABIC TO MAIN IN TWO MERGED PRs, AND MY OWN VERIFICATION WAS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF CATCHING IT. Seven ar.json values rendered as mojibake in production-bound code: admin.streams.title/help/noneWarning/save/saved (PR #264, ADR-0043 step 3) and admin.invite.streams/streamsHelp (PR #265, step 4). The Arabic UI of the StreamAssignmentPanel and the InviteUserPanel - both of which I built - displayed 'Ø§ÙÙØ³Ø§Ø±Ø§Øª' instead of 'المسارات'. Found 2026-08-14 by a delegated agent doing an unrelated task, not by any gate and not by me. ROOT CAUSE, and it is a technique error rather than a typo: I wrote the Arabic as \uXXXX escapes inside a Python heredoc and materialised them with `text.encode().decode('unicode_escape')`. `.encode()` produces UTF-8 bytes; `.decode('unicode_escape')` interprets those bytes as LATIN-1. For ASCII the two coincide, so the ENGLISH half of every identical edit came out perfect - which is exactly why the bug hid. Every non-ASCII byte was mangled. ⚠ THE SAME SESSION WROTE ARABIC CORRECTLY ELSEWHERE: the seed migration and the StreamPicker tests contain literal UTF-8 Arabic ('كل المسارات') and are intact. The defect exists only where I reached for escapes, which I did precisely because I was being careful about encoding. ⚠⚠ WHY IT SURVIVED VERIFICATION, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: after BOTH PRs I ran an i18n check and reported 'parity OK'. check-i18n.mjs compares KEY SETS, not VALUES - a mojibake value has the right key, so parity passes at 1868 keys with every Arabic string destroyed. This is the recorded memory rule 'i18n parity is not completeness' biting the person who cited it earlier in the same session. NO GATE CAN SEE THIS: not check-i18n (keys only), not tsc (a string is a string), not the unit tests (they assert on the EN locale or on ids), not the coverage gate. The only detector that would work is a value-level scan for characters outside the expected script, and it does not exist. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14, same day, in the v3.2.0 acceptance pass. All seven values rewritten as literal UTF-8 Arabic; a full-file scan for the mojibake signature returns 0; key parity re-verified at 1868 via the real check-i18n.mjs (exit 0). ⚠ THE DELEGATED AGENT CONCLUDED THE CONTENT WAS UNRECOVERABLE - 'irreversible (undefined CP1252 slots already became U+FFFD)... needs re-authoring by someone who reads Arabic'. It was right that MECHANICAL reversal fails and right to check git history, but wrong that the content was lost: the intended strings were still recoverable from the authoring calls earlier in the same session, so the repair restores what was meant rather than re-translating. A correct diagnosis of the corruption is not the same as a correct diagnosis of what is recoverable. FOLLOW-UP WORTH DOING, not done here: a value-level i18n guard that flags any ar.json value containing Latin-1 supplement characters (Ø, Ù, Û) or U+FFFD would have caught this at the commit that introduced it, and would cost about five lines beside check-i18n.mjs.

title: FIXED 2026-08-16 — THE COMMAND RAN, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THIS ROW EVER ACCEPTED AS A FIX. POST /api/members/reconcile returned HTTP 200: {identityAccounts: 27, created: 25, alreadyProvisioned: 2, skippedDisabled: 0, skippedNoCommitteeRole: 0, skippedDuplicateEmail: 0}. Verified INDEPENDENTLY by re-reading the database rather than trusting the response: committee_members went 1 -> 27 and member_streams went 1 -> 26. The status split is 2 Active / 25 Invited, which is correct by design — MembershipStatus.Invited is admin pre-registration ahead of first login, and each becomes Active when its owner signs in. ⚠ THE 27-vs-26 STREAM GAP IS NOT A DEFECT: it is the residual ReconcileIdentityAccounts.cs:33 documents in advance — 'a member who signs in BETWEEN the deploy and this run gets a JIT row with no streams, and this command will not touch it'. That member is the acmp-admin account used to obtain the token; its login created a JIT row after the backfill migration and before the reconcile, so the reconcile correctly declined to widen a row it had not created. The code predicted the exact scenario that occurred. HOW THE TOKEN WAS OBTAINED WITHOUT CREATING ANYTHING: the operator first proposed creating a throwaway committee member and then deleting it, plus deleting the audit logs so it could never orphan. The log deletion was declined on the invariant (and could not have worked — the store denies DELETE at DB-permission level and is hash-chained, so removal leaves a permanently failing verification). The creation turned out to be unnecessary: acmp-admin ALREADY existed on the prod realm holding the Administrator role, and its password had been rotated hours earlier under DEF-083. Its PKCE login JIT-provisioned the member row that, together with the role, satisfies Policies.AdminUsers. Nothing was created and nothing was deleted. ORIGINAL REPORT FOLLOWS: THE STEP-5 BACKFILL REACHES ABOUT ONE MEMBER ROW IN PRODUCTION, NOT 26 - AND DEF-062'S 'prod/UAT already hold 26 member rows' IS MY OWN ROW, WRONG IN THE SAME PLACE IT CORRECTED SOMETHING ELSE. Found 2026-08-14 while scoping the step-5 backfill, by asking WHERE a committee_members row comes from rather than trusting the count in the register. THE MEASUREMENT, four facts read from code and from an earlier live observation: (1) A committee_members row is created by exactly two paths - JIT provisioning on FIRST LOGIN (ProvisionCurrentUser.cs:49-56, ADR-0004) and MemberInvitation.InviteAsync (InviteUser for FR-156, GuestProvisioner for FR-159). (2) The 26 production accounts were seeded straight into KEYCLOAK by seed-users.sh; a Keycloak user is NOT a committee_members row, and nothing copies one into the other ahead of a login. (3) DEF-038 measured the live production roster on 2026-08-10 and it listed ONE of the 26 accounts - and that roster is GetMembersHandler reading _db.Members, so committee_members held ONE row at that observation. That is a measurement, not an inference. (4) ProvisionCurrentUser assigns NO streams - CommitteeMember.Provision takes sub/name/email/role/now and touches no stream collection. CONSEQUENCE, and it is the same outage ADR-0043 named the backfill to prevent, merely deferred: the migration assigns the wildcard to the rows existing WHEN IT RUNS - in production, about one. The other ~25 accounts have no row to reach. Each gets its row on FIRST LOGIN, with zero streams, and once step 7 wires StreamScopeRequirement each is refused every guarded write from the moment they arrive. A one-time data migration cannot close this because it cannot see Keycloak. WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM DEF-062: DEF-062 corrected the FRESH-ENVIRONMENT direction (the migration is a no-op in CI/dev because no rows exist yet) and it is right about that. Its production sentence assumed the 26 seeded ACCOUNTS were 26 member ROWS. Both rows are about the same generalisable mistake - a migration's blast radius is ROWS EXISTING AT MIGRATION TIME - and the second half of that sentence is that in production the row set is much smaller than the account set. OPTIONS: (a) accept ADR-0043 clause (2)'s stated backstop; (b) reconcile Keycloak accounts into committee_members BEFORE the step-7 deploy - DEC-046 d2 CHOSE THIS; (c) have JIT provisioning assign the wildcard - NOT RECOMMENDED per DEC-044 d2. BLAST RADIUS TODAY IS NIL AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS A PLANNING DEFECT RATHER THAN AN INCIDENT: production is unused (zero topics, one sign-in) and nothing in this stream is deployed. THE MIGRATION IS STILL CORRECT AND STILL NEEDED. ⚠⚠ STATUS 2026-08-14: THE CODE IS BUILT AND MERGED (PR #275, 9508eef) AND THIS ROW IS DELIBERATELY STILL OPEN. The chosen remedy exists, is mutation-proven and is proven on real SQL Server - but this defect's consequence is prevented only when the command actually RUNS against production at the stream-scope deploy. Closing it on merge would recreate precisely the trap this stream has already recorded once: stream scope being correct, running and evidenced is NOT the same as production being safe to deploy into. THIS ROW IS THE DEPLOY-BLOCKER TRACKER AND CLOSES WHEN THE RUN HAPPENS. WHAT DISCHARGES IT, IN ORDER: (1) set KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ENABLED=true AND pin a real KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET - two variables, not one (DEC-047 d3), and 09-put-env.sh refuses a placeholder because reconcile.sh pushes the value to the Keycloak client; (2) deploy - reconcile.sh converges the client and its grant, and NO grant change is needed because {manage-users} was MEASURED to cover the new read; (3) POST /api/members/reconcile as an Administrator IMMEDIATELY after the deploy, and check the returned partition (identityAccounts = created + alreadyProvisioned + skippedDisabled + skippedNoCommitteeRole + skippedDuplicateEmail) rather than trusting that it ran. ⚠ The Administrator token has NO CLI path - the service account is not a committee member, so its token cannot satisfy Policies.AdminUsers; sign in to the SPA as an Administrator and take the bearer token from devtools. ⚠ RESIDUAL: a member who signs in BETWEEN steps 2 and 3 gets a JIT row with no streams that the command will not touch, and falls back to clause (2)'s roster backstop - the window is minutes wide and prod has ONE sign-in in its history.

title: ASSIGNING A STREAM TO A MEMBER HAS NEVER WORKED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE - membership.member_streams.StreamId IS AN IDENTITY COLUMN, so every assignment throws 'Cannot insert explicit value for identity column'. title: FIXED 2026-08-16 IN PR #285 — AND THIS ROW'S OWN PRESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, WHICH IS WHY THE ORIGINAL TEXT IS KEPT BELOW RATHER THAN CORRECTED IN PLACE. The row predicted 'an assertion racing an async state update' and explicitly forbade a timeout. findBy*/waitFor WERE APPLIED FIRST and the failure PERSISTED — that is how the real cause was reached rather than assumed: 'Test timed out in 5000ms', failing at ~5090ms with the test still EXECUTING, not asserting against an unsettled DOM. Then a SECOND, unrelated test (RecordDecisionDialog's override-flag case) tripped the same 5s ceiling, which is what makes it a CLASS rather than one flaky test: interaction-heavy component tests under v8 coverage instrumentation on a loaded runner. Fixed ONCE in vitest.config.ts (testTimeout 15s) instead of per-test, because WHICH test trips is a function of load and pinning individual timeouts is whack-a-mole. ⚠ THIS IS NOT THE ANTI-PATTERN THE ROW WARNED ABOUT: a timeout hides a RACE by giving a racy assertion more chances to get lucky; there is no race here, every assertion still runs and still fails if the behaviour breaks. Measured 2 failures in 7 runs before, 0 in 5 after — and five clean runs is NOT claimed as proof a flake is gone; the mechanism was measured and removed. ⚠ THE LESSON THIS ROW CARRIES IS ABOUT ITSELF: a defect row's predicted cause is a hypothesis, not evidence, and following its prescribed fix without re-measuring would have left the real cause in place. ORIGINAL REPORT, PRESERVED VERBATIM: A FRONTEND TEST FAILS INTERMITTENTLY UNDER COVERAGE AND IT IS PRE-EXISTING - DecisionPage.test.tsx 'requires a condition when the successor is Conditionally Approved, then submits it'. Found 2026-08-14 while gating the AC-034 edit flow: `npm run test:cov` reported a failure that `vitest run` did not. ⚠ THE FIRST INSTINCT WAS WRONG AND WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Because the failure appeared in the same run as newly-added tests, the obvious reading was that the new work caused it. IT DID NOT: the run was repeated with every source change STASHED, and DecisionPage.test.tsx failed on the bare baseline too. Authorship was measured, not argued from plausibility. THE OBSERVATIONS: the file passes 15/15 when run ALONE, passes in a plain full `vitest run` (1206/1206, twice), and fails only under `test:cov` - and not on every coverage run, which is what makes it flaky rather than broken. Coverage instrumentation slows every test in the process, so this is the classic load-sensitive async assertion: the same shape as DEF-061 on the e2e side and the same class as the recorded 'localhost CI hides load races' finding. A developer machine settles the interaction before the assertion and never sees it; a loaded runner does not. WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE BEING LOW: `test:cov` is what CI's frontend job runs, so this can turn an unrelated PR red, and an intermittently red gate is how a blocking check becomes something people re-run without reading - the exact failure mode this project has already recorded for advisories. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY: it is unrelated to the ADR-0043 slice and to AC-034, and folding an unrelated test fix into that PR would hide it. FIX WHEN PICKED UP: read the assertion before changing it - the likely shape is an assertion racing an async state update, and the repair is to await the settled state (findBy*/waitFor) rather than to add a timeout or a retry, both of which would hide a genuine regression the day one occurs.

title: STEP 7's BLAST RADIUS WAS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT DEF-062 PREDICTED, AND THE REAL LANDMINE WAS A TEST STUB, NOT THE E2E SUITE. Measured 2026-08-14 after step 6 merged, by grepping every path that reaches Policies.TopicEdit instead of reasoning about which environments the change touches. ⚠ WHAT DEF-062 SAID: 'at step 7 every e2e fixture holding a stream-bounded role is refused every guarded write - the whole core-loop and every spec that submits, edits or acts on a topic as a Member.' THAT WAS WRONG, and it was wrong because it reasoned from ROLES rather than from CALL SITES. THE MEASUREMENT, four facts: (1) Policies.TopicEdit is the ONLY stream-bounded policy evaluated WITH a resource - TopicTriage and BacklogPrioritize allow Chairman/Secretary only (who bypass), TopicSubmit is endpoint-level with no resource at all, and DiagramAttach has no EnsureAsync call site anywhere. (2) Every e2e caller of a TopicEdit-gated route is a SECRETARY: apiHelpers.prepareTopic passes the secretary bearer (its own comment says so), scenario.ts prepares with the secretary, core-loop.spec.ts marks Prepared through the Secretary's UI session, and ac049-upload-l10n.spec.ts uploads attachments as loginAs(page,'secretary'). (3) topic-scope.spec.ts's Member assertions ALREADY EXPECT 403 - so they stayed green, though for a second reason. (4) Acmp.Api.Tests' TopicEdit paths are the submitter editing pre-Accept (no authorization at all) or a Secretary. ✅ CI SETTLED IT EMPIRICALLY: PR #269 wired the requirement and the e2e job PASSED. ⚠ THE ACTUAL LANDMINE, and it failed CLOSED and LOUDLY rather than open: PermissionMatrixTests evaluates every registered policy against `StubTopic : ITopicScopedResource`, which does NOT implement IStreamScopedResource, AND it evaluates the 'A' cells with NO RESOURCE AT ALL. StreamScopeHandler is AuthorizationHandler<StreamScopeRequirement, IStreamScopedResource>, and ASP.NET never invokes a two-parameter handler when the resource is absent or of the wrong type - so the requirement went unsatisfied and EVERY TopicEdit cell flipped to Deny, the Chairman and Secretary Allow cells included. Confirmed by running it, not by predicting it. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #269 (squash 1f0cbcd) - and NOT by making the stub satisfy the requirement and moving on, which is the wrong lesson. The stub was only the messenger: the same shape refuses ANY call site passing a non-stream-scoped resource. So the test now ASSERTS THE REAL PROPERTY - a stream-scoped policy is RESOURCE-ONLY and cannot be decided without a resource - and AuthorizationRegistration.StreamScoped carries the rule for adding a policy to that set: only where every call site passes a stream-scoped aggregate. The stub implements IStreamScopedResource with a stream the principal holds, so the matrix test stays about the CAPABILITY matrix (§C) instead of silently becoming a stream-scope test (§E.1). GENERALISABLE, and it was the third instance of this class in one slice: a REQUIREMENT typed to a RESOURCE is invisible wherever that resource type is absent - at endpoint-level evaluation (no resource), at a call site with a different aggregate, and in a test stub. ALSO CARRIED AND USED: AC-010's discrimination is reachable through PrepareTopic and essentially nowhere else - UpdateTopic pre-Accept skips authorization for the submitter and refuses a non-owner Member on the CAPABILITY check before streams are consulted, and post-Accept it uses TopicTriage. That analysis is what step 8's fixture was built on (d94f154).

title: RUNNING THE COVERAGE GATE LOCALLY MORE THAN ONCE MADE IT REPORT ON CODE THAT NO LONGER EXISTED - check-coverage.mjs merged EVERY cobertura report under tests/*/TestResults, and `dotnet test --collect` writes a NEW timestamped directory on every run instead of replacing the last one. Found 2026-08-14 during ADR-0043 step 7, and it cost two speculative changes before it was caught. THE SYMPTOM: the gate failed with `50.00% (1/2) AbacProviders.cs` and kept failing with the identical figure after the only coverable code in that file had been MOVED OUT of it. A file with no code cannot be 50% covered, which is what made the measurement suspect rather than the code. THE MEASUREMENT: 30 TestResults directories had accumulated across one session's repeated runs; the script walked the tree from the repo root and summed every coverage.cobertura.xml it found, so a file edited between runs was scored against its OLD self as well as its new one and the worst historical reading won. Deleting tests/*/TestResults and re-running turned the same commit from FAIL to PASS. ⚠ CI WAS UNAFFECTED, which is exactly why it survived: every CI run starts from a fresh checkout with no TestResults at all, so the gate was correct there and wrong only on the machine of anyone following the project's own standing advice to run the gates locally before pushing. ⚠ A STALE GATE DOES NOT MERELY WASTE TIME, IT DIRECTS WORK: two changes were made to satisfy the false reading before the reading itself was doubted. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #273 (squash d42ae7c) per DEC-047: the script now takes only the NEWEST report per test project and logs how many it ignored. Keyed on the TestResults parent, so a solution-wide run still measures every project - just once each, at its latest run. ⚠ THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS WRONG AND ITS OWN LOG LINE CAUGHT IT, which is worth recording because the failure mode is the same class as the defect: the grouping key split the path on a hand-written /[\/]/ character class, which matches FORWARD SLASHES ONLY, while node's join() produces BACKSLASHES on Windows. Every key collapsed to the empty string, all five reports landed in one bucket, four legitimate per-project reports were discarded, and the gate reported 84.70% - a FALSE FAILURE, which is worse than the stale reading it replaced. It announced 'ignoring 4 superseded report(s)', and that line - added on instinct so the reader would be told rather than silently given a merge - is the only reason the failure was diagnosable rather than mysterious. Replaced with dirname twice, which has no separator to hand-write. VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a clean full run reports 99.61% and ignores nothing; a planted stale duplicate with an older mtime is ignored rather than merged.

Caught 2026-08-14 in the act, while rebasing fix/admin-streams-tab-live onto main under DEC-046. Arabic encoded UTF-8 then decoded as Latin-1 always lands in the Ø/Ù/Ã block, and correct Arabic never contains those characters at all - so ONE is enough, with no threshold to tune and no way for a partially corrupted string to slip under it. title: DEC-046's RECONCILIATION IS INERT FOR DEF-065 UNLESS IT ASSIGNS THE WILDCARD ITSELF - creating the member rows is necessary and NOT sufficient, because the backfill that would have covered them has already run by then. Found 2026-08-14 while scoping the reconciliation, by asking WHEN the migration runs relative to WHEN reconciliation would create rows. ⚠ THE DECISION IS NOT WRONG - ITS MECHANISM IS ONE CLAUSE SHORT. DEC-046 chose to 'reconcile Keycloak accounts into committee_members BEFORE the step-7 deploy, so the rows exist for the backfill to reach', and that is the right shape. The gap is in the word BEFORE: reconciliation is an APPLICATION FEATURE, so it can only run on a host that is already up - and Program.cs:133 applies migrations at BOOT, before the first HTTP request is served. The deploy that carries the reconciliation feature therefore also carries and RUNS the step-5 backfill first, against whatever rows exist at that moment, which is the same ~1 row DEF-065 describes. An administrator then reconciles, creating ~25 rows with ZERO streams - each of which is stream-bounded, and every one of them is refused every guarded write from their first login. That is exactly the outcome DEF-065 exists to prevent, reached by a different route. THE MEASUREMENT: Program.cs:133 runs MigrationRunner.MigrateAsync(app) during startup; the only two paths that write member_streams are AssignStreamsHandler (the Administrator-only PUT) and InviteUserHandler, and neither is part of any reconciliation. So nothing between 'row created by reconciliation' and 'member signs in' assigns a stream. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: the reconciliation command must assign the WILDCARD to every row IT CREATES - doing precisely what the backfill would have done had the row existed - rather than leaving assignment to a separate administrative step. ⚠ IT MUST APPLY ONLY TO ROWS IT CREATES, never to rows that already exist: an administrator may have deliberately narrowed someone to one stream, and widening that to the wildcard on a reconciliation run would silently hand them universal write access. This is the same asymmetry the step-5 backfill already encodes with its NOT EXISTS clause, and the reconciliation should encode it the same way. ⚠ A SECOND, SEPARATE OBSTACLE, recorded here so it is not discovered halfway: IIdentityProvider HAS NO READ OPERATION. Its four methods are CreateUser, SetRealmRoles, SignOutEverywhere and DisableUser, and its own comment states the narrowness is deliberate - 'no general-purpose call-Keycloak escape hatch, so the blast radius of the service-account credential is bounded by this interface'. Reconciliation needs to LIST realm users with their roles, which is a fifth operation on an ADR-0038-governed port. A bounded READ is consistent with that rationale (a read cannot mutate the identity provider) but it is a real widening of a surface that was narrowed on purpose, and it should be recorded as such rather than slipped in. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 by PR #275 (9508eef), built from the corrected mechanism rather than discovering the gap afterwards. BOTH clauses are implemented and BOTH are mutation-proven: creating the row and granting the wildcard are ONE operation in ReconcileIdentityAccountsHandler, and the grant applies only to rows that run creates. The port widening was recorded as SC-011 BEFORE the interface change existed in code. ⚠ THE ASYMMETRY NEEDED A TEST THAT DID NOT EXIST AT FIRST REVIEW: 'wildcard everyone' is caught by a member narrowed to one stream, but the subtler wrong implementation - 'wildcard any member holding ZERO streams' - was caught by NOTHING, because no test carried a pre-existing zero-stream member. That is the plausible later 'fix', and it is wrong for a reason invisible from the data: an administrator can clear a member's streams deliberately and member_streams has no provenance column to tell the two apart. It is now pinned by Reconcile_leaves_a_pre_existing_member_holding_NO_streams_alone, which is the sole test that mutant fails.

Found 2026-08-14 by running gate_run() after recording DEF-041's fix - the gate went from 7/7 to fail with three findings, all of them rows I had just written. WHAT HAPPENED: ACMP Administration.dc.html is a template, so the control it draws appears in the file as an element whose click handler is a mustache expression. Quoting that verbatim into two progress entries and a defect title was the natural way to evidence the INV-014 finding about where the voting toggle belongs. G-COMPLETE screens content for unfinished-work markers, and its pattern list ends with an empty mustache expression - the very token an unfinished template leaves behind - so faithfully quoted evidence and an unfinished document are indistinguishable to it. THE MEASUREMENT, not a guess: tamheed_server.py defines the screen as the usual unfinished-work words plus an angle-bracket filler token, a mustache expression and a filler-text phrase; the call site strips code spans FIRST, with a comment saying such markers inside code spans are example text rather than unfinished markers. So the escape is designed and documented in the source: BACKTICK ANY QUOTED TEMPLATE SYNTAX. WHY IT WAS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: progress_entries is an APPEND-ONLY JOURNAL. entity_upsert on an existing PE- id is refused by a UNIQUE constraint whose error message says corrections are recorded as new entries, not edits - correct design, and exactly why the mistake was expensive. A defect TITLE is mutable and was simply rewritten; two progress entries were not. HOW IT WAS REPAIRED, through the sanctioned path rather than by hand: the runtime store is an always-fresh in-memory SQLite rebuilt from the canonical JSONL on every open (store.py), and the recorded procedure for a bad write is 'rollback is git only'. So: package_close to release and flush, a WHOLE-FILE git checkout of progress_entries.jsonl at the last commit before the bad entries, package_open to rebuild the store from the restored file, then re-append the entries with the template token in backticks. That is a whole-file git rollback, not a hand-edit of package data; it left PE-325..PE-327 untouched and reallocated the same ids to the corrected entries, so no gap appears. ⚠ AND THE FIX ITSELF TRIPPED THE GATE ONCE MORE, which is the funniest and most useful part of this row: the FIRST version of this very title spelled out the marker words it was describing, so a defect ABOUT the placeholder screen was caught BY the placeholder screen. Describing a pattern counts as writing it. ⚠ THE GENERAL LESSON IS NOT ABOUT MUSTACHES: the package is PROSE ABOUT CODE, so any syntax quoted into it is read by the gates as if it were the package's own text. Code-span every quoted fragment. ⚠ AND THE SHARPER ONE: run gate_run() AFTER writing, not only before. Had I closed the session on the merge, main would have carried a red critical gate with the failing rows immutable, and the next session would have inherited both.

title: FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-15. JIT PROVISIONING HAD A CHECK-THEN-INSERT RACE: POST /api/members/me is documented idempotent by the SPA and by the e2e helpers, and was not - two simultaneous calls for a subject with no member row both INSERT and the loser got a 500. MEASURED FROM THE API LOG: DbUpdateException wrapping SqlException 'Cannot insert duplicate key row in object membership.committee_members with unique index IX_committee_members_KeycloakUserId', logged twice for one subject within the same second. It can ONLY collide on a subject's FIRST provisioning; in e2e a run's first login was historically driven by ac043-reorder.spec.ts, which never calls meMember, so exactly one provisioning call was ever in flight. ac011-guest-scope is the first spec to call roleSession at the START of a run. The race was always present and had simply never been occupied - and the harness was not the defect, since it calls an endpoint that advertises idempotency. MY FIRST ANALYSIS WAS WRONG AND WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT (PE-350 corrects PE-348): I asserted the fix HAD to retry the whole command above TransactionBehavior because the ambient transaction would be doomed. A unique violation aborts the STATEMENT, not the transaction (XACT_ABORT is off), so the transaction is intact and commits normally; and SQL Server does not fail the loser immediately - it BLOCKS on the winner's key lock and raises the duplicate only once that transaction has COMMITTED, which is what makes the loser's re-read GUARANTEED rather than hopeful. FIX (PR #279, 3a27fef): the loser detaches its own pending insert, re-reads, adopts the winner's row and syncs claims onto it; a DbUpdateException with no winning row behind it is rethrown unchanged. Four tests, every guard mutation-proven with each mutant confirmed to compile: removing the recovery kills 3, removing the detach kills 1, absorbing a non-race failure kills 1, letting the loser still report created kills 1. The race is SIMULATED rather than run, deliberately: the InMemory provider does not enforce unique indexes, so a genuinely concurrent test there would pass whether or not the fix existed - the DEF-066 shape exactly. VERIFIED ON A REAL DATABASE by the AC-011 e2e leg going green (run 31895092054): the 500 that produced this defect no longer occurs. title: FIXED 2026-08-16, MERGED IN PR #286 (0a747ff), THEN IMMEDIATELY AMENDED BY THE OPERATOR — and the amendment is the part worth reading. Both compose files now probe /readyz instead of /healthz, so the container health signal is honest. ⚠ BUT REPOINTING IT ALSO MADE READINESS A STARTUP INTERLOCK: web and worker both declared depends_on api condition:service_healthy, so a blip in SQL Server, Hangfire or object storage would have stopped the stack from starting at all — a degraded stack turned into a total outage. That consequence was not on the table when DEC-056 d2 was decided; it was measured afterwards, put back to the operator, and they chose to keep the signal and drop the gate. All four dependencies are now service_started (fd98515). ⚠ The row also sat Open after merging, same two-part obligation failure as DEF-078. ORIGINAL REPORT FOLLOWS: THE API CONTAINER'S HEALTHCHECK EVALUATES NOTHING, SO IT HAS REPORTED 'healthy' FOR THREE DAYS WHILE /readyz RETURNED 503 — A LIVENESS PROBE STANDING IN FOR A READINESS PROBE. Measured 2026-08-16 on production: `docker ps` shows acmp-cloud-api-1 as 'Up 3 days (healthy)' at the same moment `curl http://localhost:8080/readyz` inside that container returns HTTP 503, body 'Unhealthy'. THE MECHANISM, read not inferred: docker-compose.cloud.yml:256 defines the api healthcheck as `curl -f http://localhost:8080/healthz`, and Program.cs:109 maps /healthz with `Predicate = _ => false`. A predicate of `_ => false` selects ZERO registered checks, so the endpoint returns 200 unconditionally as long as the process can accept a TCP connection and route a request. The healthcheck therefore CANNOT fail for any application reason — not a dead database, not an unreachable object store, not a broken Hangfire schema. It is structurally incapable of detecting the condition it appears to cover. ⚠ THIS IS WHY DEF-078 WENT UNNOTICED FOR THREE DAYS, AND THAT IS THE REAL COST: the 503 was not hidden by subtlety, it was hidden because the only indicator anyone LOOKS AT was wired to the endpoint that knows nothing. This is the ninth instance in this project of the recorded pattern 'a control must DETECT and TELL' — and here the detect half is the missing one, which is the rarer and worse variant. ⚠ IT HAS NOT CAUSED AN OUTAGE ONLY BY LUCK OF TOPOLOGY, which is why the severity is medium rather than high: there is no ALB, no orchestrator and no autoscaler consuming /readyz in this deployment, so nothing pulls the instance out of rotation on a 503. The day one is introduced, this inverts — a 503 readiness endpoint takes production out at the first health sweep while `docker ps` still reads green for the operator watching it. THE FIX (DEC-056 d2): repoint the compose healthcheck at /readyz. ⚠⚠ SEQUENCING IS MANDATORY AND IS PART OF THE DEFECT: this MUST land AFTER the DEF-078 probe fix. Repointing first would mark the api container unhealthy the moment it is applied, because /readyz is 503 TODAY, risking restart churn on a live stack. ⚠ ALSO CHECK THE SIBLINGS BEFORE CLOSING: web (docker-compose.cloud.yml:183) probes http://localhost/health and worker has no healthcheck at all — neither was measured here, and assuming they are correct because this one was found would repeat the error that produced this row.

title: FIXED 2026-08-17 — ROTATED, which is the only thing that revokes a credential already public in git history. The UAT instance was started for the purpose, the four seed accounts (chairman, secretary, member, auditor) were each reset via kcadm to a DIFFERENT fresh TEMPORARY password, and the instance was stopped again. requiredActions=[UPDATE_PASSWORD] was re-read for all four rather than assumed, so each value is single-use by construction — which matters because an SSM command's output is retained in AWS, and a single-use credential in a log is worthless the moment its owner signs in. ⚠ FOUR DIFFERENT PASSWORDS, NOT ONE SHARED VALUE: the original defect was a single password shared across four accounts and then written into five files. Restoring that shape would have re-created the thing being fixed. ⚠ NOT VERIFIED BY LOGGING IN, AND THE REASON IS THE SAME ONE THAT APPLIED ON PRODUCTION: a temporary password is consumed by the login that tests it, so proving it works destroys it and leaves the operator holding a dead credential. The evidence is kcadm's own confirmation plus the re-read requiredActions, which is one layer below the login rather than absent. ⚠ SIDE FINDING, RECORDED BECAUSE NOBODY WAS LOOKING FOR IT: the UAT realm still carries probe litter — kc-grant-probe@acmp.local and two probe.invite.20260812*@acmp.local accounts left behind by earlier one-off probes, alongside the four known e2e-* fixtures. Not a live exposure while the instance is stopped, but test-run artefacts accumulating in an identity realm is how a forgotten enabled account eventually becomes one. ORIGINAL REPORT FOLLOWS: THE UAT SEED-ACCOUNT PASSWORD WAS HARD-CODED IN FIVE TRACKED FILES AND IS STILL LIVE IN GIT HISTORY. Found 2026-08-16 while searching the repo for deploy hostnames, which is to say it was found BY ACCIDENT. WHAT WAS EXPOSED: the rotated password for the four UAT seed accounts, as a plaintext literal in src/Acmp.Web/uat-login-probe.mjs, src/Acmp.Web/uat-invite-probe.mjs, handoff/RESUME-ph5-closeout.md, handoff/RESUME-ph5-sl025.md, and .claude/memory/ph5-sl025-uat-live.md. ⚠ THE LAST ONE IS THE WORST: that memory file is auto-loaded into agent context at the start of EVERY session, so the credential was being re-read continuously by an assistant, indefinitely, with no action by anyone. ⚠⚠ THE COMMENT DEFENDING IT WAS THE ACTUAL DEFECT: uat-login-probe.mjs carried 'Not a secret: these are UAT fixtures on a throwaway environment, and the value never leaves this file'. The second clause was FALSE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN — a single grep found five copies. 'It never leaves this file' is not a property you can assert; it is one you can only measure, and nobody measured it. A rationalisation attached to a hard-coded credential is how the credential earns permanent residency: every later reader sees that the question was already considered and moves on. ⚠ THIS ROW ALSO FIRST CLAIMED 'no secret-scanning gate flagged it', AND THAT WAS FALSE — gitleaks runs gating over FULL history and passed on 153 commits because it allowlisted every .md file by path (DEF-081). The wrong sentence is kept in the record because a confident absence-claim written from a quick look is exactly the failure this project keeps recording.

title: FIXED 2026-08-16 (b96bf9b). The '''.*\.md''' path allowlist is gone; the two historic findings are held by FINGERPRINT (commit+file+rule+line), which is the only legitimate way to carry a real leak here — and the file's own rule was obeyed rather than bypassed, because DEF-083 ROTATED the live credential first. A fingerprint pins one occurrence, so the same secret in a NEW commit gets a different fingerprint and still fails the gate. ⚠ MY OWN SIZING CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: I told the operator this would 'go green immediately because the file is scrubbed'. gitleaks scans git HISTORY, so scrubbing the working tree changes nothing — the findings are permanent. ⚠ AND THE FIRST VERIFICATION WAS FAULTY IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION: planting a secret in a .md produced NO new finding, which looked like the fix had failed. It had not — the planted value was an AWS docs example key that matches no rule. Planting the SAME value in a .txt as a CONTROL proved it was detectable, and then .md caught it too: baseline 11 -> .txt 12 -> .md 12. Without the control I would have concluded the fix did not work and reverted it. ⚠ THIS ROW WAS ALSO LEFT OPEN AFTER THE FIX COMMITTED — the THIRD such lapse today after DEF-067 and DEF-078/079, all the same half-discharged two-part obligation, and none of them caught by a gate. ORIGINAL REPORT FOLLOWS: THE GITLEAKS SECRET-SCANNING GATE IS BLIND TO EVERY MARKDOWN FILE IN THE REPOSITORY, BY A ONE-LINE PATH ALLOWLIST — AND THAT IS HOW A PLAINTEXT CREDENTIAL SURVIVED 153 GATED COMMITS. Found 2026-08-16 immediately after DEF-080, by checking a claim rather than trusting it: DEF-080 asserted there was no secret-scanning gate, and there is one. THE CONTROL IS REAL AND WELL-BUILT: .github/workflows/security.yml runs ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks:v8.21.2 with `detect --config=/repo/.gitleaks.toml --redact --verbose --exit-code=1` and `fetch-depth: 0`, so it scans FULL history and FAILS the build on a finding. It is not advisory and it is not shallow. THE HOLE IS .gitleaks.toml LINE 13: the allowlist contains `paths = ['''.*\.md''']` with the comment 'docs may quote example values'. That is not an exemption for a documentation folder — it exempts EVERY markdown file anywhere in the repository, forever, by path, so the VALUE inside is never examined at all. Three of DEF-080's five leak sites were .md, including .claude/memory/ph5-sl025-uat-live.md, which is auto-loaded into agent context every session. The scan could not have caught them at any point. ⚠ THE FILE'S OWN HEADER FORBIDS EXACTLY THIS AND WAS OVERTAKEN BY IT: line 2 reads 'A genuine finding outside this allowlist is a real leak — rotate the credential; do NOT just add it here.' The discipline is correct and it is aimed at the REGEX list, where each entry is a specific triaged value. The PATH list silently does something categorically different: a value-based allowlist exempts one known string, a path-based one exempts every string that will ever be written in that location. The two sit under one heading and read as the same kind of thing. ⚠ THE OTHER TWO SITES WERE .mjs AND ALSO SURVIVED, which is a SECOND and separate gap: no path rule covered them, so gitleaks' default ruleset simply did not match a bare quoted literal assigned to a NEW_PASSWORD constant. Any fix that only narrows the .md path leaves that half open, and a fix verified solely against the .md case would look complete while proving nothing about the .mjs one. ⚠ THIS IS THE TENTH INSTANCE OF 'A CONTROL MUST DETECT AND TELL' IN THIS PROJECT AND THE SECOND FOUND TODAY, after DEF-079's container healthcheck. Both are the same shape: a control that is present, green, trusted, and structurally unable to see the thing it is believed to cover.

title: EIGHT PUBLIC AGGREGATE METHODS ARE REACHABLE FROM NO PRODUCTION CODE PATH — THE SIXTH FIRING OF DW-026, AND THE FIRST TO CATCH MORE THAN ONE AT A TIME. Found 2026-08-17 by the broad reachability check built for DW-026 (PR #288), which walks the IL of every method in every production assembly, collects its call targets, and reports aggregate methods absent from that set. THE EIGHT, each verified BY HAND to have no caller outside its own Domain assembly rather than trusted from the tool that reported them: Topic::Close/3, Topic::Convert/3, Topic::Reactivate/3, Topic::Reclassify/2, Topic::Reopen/4, CommitteeMember::HasExpired/1, CommitteeMember::Reactivate/0, Delegation::IsActiveAt/1. WHAT THIS CLASS OF DEFECT IS, restated because the count now argues for it: a capability that exists, compiles, is often unit-tested and passing, and is wired to nothing. Its previous five instances included SetVotingEligibility, which sat uncalled from P4 until PR #276 while its own unit tests passed the whole time — a unit test calls the method DIRECTLY, which is exactly why no test suite can detect this. ⚠ THE FIVE TOPIC METHODS ARE THE INTERESTING GROUP: Close, Convert, Reactivate, Reclassify and Reopen are topic LIFECYCLE transitions, so the aggregate models a richer lifecycle than any endpoint or handler exposes. That is not automatically a bug — domain modelling ahead of surface is legitimate — but it is exactly the state where a reader assumes a capability is available because the method exists. Each needs a decision: wire it to a use case, or record that it is deliberately unexposed. ⚠ HasExpired and IsActiveAt ARE PREDICATES, AND PREDICATES THAT NOTHING CALLS DESERVE A SECOND LOOK: a time-window predicate that is never evaluated is the shape of a guard that was written and then bypassed, which is the family DEF-052 and ADR-0039 already record for this project. Worth checking whether an equivalent check exists elsewhere in a less obvious form. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY: these are eight independent product decisions about whether a capability should be exposed, and PR #288 exists to STOP THE NUMBER GROWING rather than to make the existing eight disappear. They are seeded into that test's allowlist, each carrying this defect id, so the guard is green on today's known set and fails on anything new. Remove an entry from the allowlist when its capability is wired up.

title: A DISABLED MEMBER IS PERMANENTLY LOCKED OUT — THERE IS NO REACTIVATION PATH ANYWHERE IN THE PRODUCT, AND THE HOURLY SWEEP CREATES THIS STATE BY ITSELF. Split out of DEF-084 by DEC-057 d1 as the one of its eight findings that is not domain-modelling-ahead-of-surface but the MISSING HALF OF A SHIPPED TWO-WAY OPERATION. THE ASYMMETRY, measured: CommitteeMember.Deactivate() has TWO production callers — DeactivateMember.cs:42, behind the admin's POST /api/members/{publicId}/deactivate, and ExpireGuestAccess.cs:74, the HOURLY guest-expiry sweep. CommitteeMember.Reactivate() has NONE: there is no ReactivateMember feature under Membership.Application/Features and no reactivate endpoint in MembershipEndpoints.cs (deactivate, roles, voting-eligibility, streams, invite, reconcile and delegations are all there). ⚠ RE-INVITING IS NOT A WORKAROUND, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT A LOCKOUT RATHER THAN AN INCONVENIENCE: MemberInvitation.InviteAsync:50 throws 'A member with the email {email} already exists' on ANY existing member row REGARDLESS of status, and BOTH invite paths route through that one helper — InviteUser.cs:68 and GuestProvisioner.cs:47. So the ordinary re-admission gesture fails with a duplicate error. ⚠ NOR IS DELETION AVAILABLE: this project's standing rule is disable-never-delete, because deleting the Keycloak user ORPHANS the member rows forever (the immutable-history asymmetry). title: THE WORKER csproj's BASE-IMAGE JUSTIFICATION IS STALE AND WOULD MISLEAD THE NEXT DECISION. src/Acmp.Worker/Acmp.Worker.csproj justifies using GRANULAR Serilog packages rather than Serilog.AspNetCore with this reasoning: 'this is a headless daemon on the slim dotnet/runtime:8.0 base, and Serilog.AspNetCore carries a FrameworkReference to Microsoft.AspNetCore.App that isn't present in that image (would crash at startup)'. BOTH HALVES ARE FALSE TODAY. (1) The worker does not ship on that base: deploy/Dockerfile.backend's `worker` target is FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 - the same digest-pinned image as the `api` target - so Microsoft.AspNetCore.App IS present. (2) The framework reference is there anyway: the built src/Acmp.Worker/bin/Release/net8.0/Acmp.Worker.runtimeconfig.json lists Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 8.0.0 among its frameworks, resolved transitively through Acmp.Bootstrap and the module graph, with no AspNetCore package named in the worker's own csproj. WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SILENT COMMENT FIX: the note is not decoration, it is a stated CONSTRAINT that shapes future package choices, and it nearly shaped one. While wiring DW-062 I excluded OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore from this host partly on the strength of it. The exclusion happens to remain correct for an unrelated and better reason - the worker serves no HTTP, so inbound-request instrumentation has nothing to instrument - but the reasoning I was handed was wrong, and the next agent could equally be steered AWAY from a package that is in fact perfectly safe here, or toward believing the image is smaller and more locked-down than it is. A false constraint is more expensive than a missing one. title: NFR-054's 500 MB CAP IS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN, AND ITS MINIMAL-BASE CLAUSE IS UNMET BY TWO MORE IMAGES - MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED. NFR-054 (Must, Approved) reads: 'Container images shall be built from a minimal base image (e.g. mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0-alpine or equivalent distroless); image size shall not exceed 500 MB. Target: Image size <= 500 MB.' ACMP publishes four image kinds. MEASURED: web 51.1 MB, worker 245 MB, api 257 MB, sqlserver-fts 3.62 GB - consistent across five CI-built commit tags spanning two weeks, so these are shipped numbers and not one build's noise. THE SIZE CLAUSE FAILS ON sqlserver-fts BY 7.2x AND CANNOT BE MADE TO PASS. Its base image, mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest, is 1.67 GB by itself - already 3.3x the cap before ACMP adds anything - and what ACMP adds is the Full-Text Search package that AC-061 and FR-143/145 require for Arabic and English search, installed with --no-install-recommends and followed by an apt clean-up. There is no smaller official SQL Server image. So no change to this Dockerfile can satisfy the requirement; only changing the requirement, or not shipping SQL Server as a container, can. THE MINIMAL-BASE CLAUSE FAILS SEPARATELY AND ON DIFFERENT IMAGES: web genuinely is minimal (nginx-unprivileged alpine), but api and worker build FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0, which is Debian-based and neither alpine nor distroless - while passing the size cap by a wide margin at 257 and 245 MB. So the two clauses are violated by disjoint sets of images and cannot be dispositioned as one thing. WHY THIS IS A DEFECT ROW AND NOT A DEFERRED-WORK ROW: nothing is going to be built. This is the register asserting something untrue about shipped reality, which is the same class as DEF-012 and DEF-095 - and a Must-priority requirement that no achievable change can satisfy will otherwise sit Approved forever, unverifiable and unfalsifiable. THE DISPOSITIONS, ALL OPERATOR-ONLY: (a) narrow NFR-054 by scope change to the APPLICATION images, naming the database image as excluded and why - the SC-023 shape, and the closest fit to what the requirement plainly meant; (b) keep the cap and record a deliberate accepted divergence for the database image; (c) treat the minimal-base clause separately and decide whether api and worker should move to alpine or distroless, which is a real deployment risk and NOT implied by either of the first two. ⚠ DO NOT CHANGE ANY BASE IMAGE TO CLOSE THIS ROW WITHOUT THAT DECISION - alpine is musl rather than glibc, and SQL Server client libraries and globalization behaviour are exactly the areas that break.

title: TWO TEST CLASSES REGISTER A PROCESS-GLOBAL ActivityListener ON THE SAME SOURCE AND EACH ASSERTS ContainSingle(), SO THEY RECORD EACH OTHER'S SPANS. HangfireJobTracingFilterTests (Bootstrap) and HangfireWebexJobSchedulerTests (Webex) each call ActivitySource.AddActivityListener on AcmpTelemetry.SourceName inside a Listen() helper, collect every stopped activity into a local list, and then assert recorded.Should().ContainSingle(). An ActivityListener is PROCESS-GLOBAL - there is no per-test scoping in System.Diagnostics - and xUnit parallelises across test classes, so whenever the two listener windows overlap each list receives the other class's spans and ContainSingle() fails. OBSERVED, NOT THEORISED: running the full Acmp.Application.Tests suite, Enqueue_emits_a_producer_dispatch_span_naming_the_job_type failed having recorded 'hangfire.execute SampleJob.RunAsync' (Consumer, from the OTHER class) beside its own 'hangfire.dispatch Enqueue'. It reproduced ONCE IN EIGHT full-suite runs - main measured green 4 of 4 and the feature branch green 4 of 4 after the single failure - which is the worst frequency a flake can have: often enough to redden main at random, rare enough for the next session to dismiss it as noise and re-run. WHY IT APPEARED NOW: both classes were created by batch 13 (DW-062 and its PR #297 follow-on), so this has been latent since 2026-08-20 and the first suite run that happened to overlap them was this one. WORTH NAMING SEPARATELY: Dispatching_with_nobody_listening_costs_no_activity_and_still_enqueues is among the affected tests. It asserts that with NO listener registered StartJobDispatch returns null - a claim that a sibling class registering a global listener silently makes FALSE, so that test can pass or fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the code it names. THE FIX: put both classes in the existing DisableParallelization collection (HangfireServerCollection, already owned by WebexJobDeadLetterTests) rather than adding a second mechanism. This is COMPLETE rather than a mitigation: AcmpTelemetry has exactly two StartActivity call sites (hangfire.dispatch, hangfire.execute) and exactly two test classes register a listener, so no other test in the repository can emit a span on this source. PROVEN TO HAVE TEETH, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERED: a green suite over a timing flake is not evidence, so the overlap was FORCED by holding each listener open 400 ms. Without the collection attributes FIVE tests fail; with them and the identical probe, 1133 pass. The probe was then removed and the suite re-run clean.

title: OTLP TRACES HAVE NEVER REACHED Seq IN ANY ENVIRONMENT: THE EXPORTER DEFAULTS TO gRPC AND POSTS TO A PATH Seq RETURNS 404 FOR. MEASURED ON A RUNNING STACK, NOT INFERRED. Both deploy/docker-compose.yml and deploy/docker-compose.cloud.yml set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to http://seq:5341/ingest/otlp and NEITHER SETS OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL - which is set nowhere in the repository at all. The OpenTelemetry .NET OTLP exporter defaults to the grpc protocol, which posts to the configured endpoint VERBATIM; the http/protobuf protocol appends the signal path. Probed directly against a running Seq: POST /ingest/otlp returns 404, POST /ingest/otlp/v1/traces returns 200. So the shipped configuration sends every trace to a path that does not exist, and the OpenTelemetry SDK swallows export failures by design unless its self-diagnostic log is enabled, which it is not. THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, because a count alone would not have shown this: with the shipped configuration, eight /readyz calls grew Seq's event count from 679 to 739 - the Serilog log path works perfectly - while the DB span count stayed at EXACTLY 72 with an unchanged newest-span timestamp. The log pipeline and the trace pipeline share a host, a port and a container, and one delivers while the other does not. Setting OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL to http/protobuf and restarting the api made spans appear immediately: 51 DB spans carrying db.query.text, db.system, server.address, plus AspNetCore Server spans and outbound HTTP Client spans to minio. WHAT THIS COSTS. Batch 13 built the DB, outbound-HTTP and job-dispatch instrumentation (PR #296) and the Hangfire job-execution filter (PR #297), and AC-133 records NFR-043 as Met on the strength of spans being GENERATED. They are generated. They are then dropped in transit, in every environment including UAT and production, which use the identical endpoint string. Any future instruction to check the traces would have found nothing and been unable to tell an empty pipeline from a quiet one. THIS IS ALSO THE REAL EXPLANATION OF DW-065. That row says no trace has ever been OBSERVED and has been carried for several batches as though it were a matter of nobody having looked. Nobody could have looked: nothing ever arrived. THE FIX IS ONE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE in both compose files - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL set to http/protobuf on api and worker - and the honest alternative is appending /v1/traces to the endpoint, which is worse because the metrics exporter needs /v1/metrics and a single base plus the protocol setting handles both. SEVERITY high, and stated deliberately rather than softened: nothing malfunctions for a user and no data is lost, but a shipped observability capability is 100 percent non-functional in production, an acceptance criterion rests on work whose output never arrives, and the next agent told to read a trace would have been debugging a pipeline nobody had ever proven end to end. VERIFY THE FIX BY THE SAME DISCRIMINATOR, not by a green start-up: send traffic, and assert the DB span count MOVES.

title: NFR-019 REQUIRES TLS ON THREE INTERNAL HOPS AND TWO OF THEM RUN IN PLAINTEXT BY DESIGN; THE THIRD DOES NOT EXIST. NFR-019 (Must, Approved) reads: 'All inter-service communication (application to SQL Server, application to Tarseem sidecar, application to Keycloak) shall use TLS 1.2 or higher; TLS 1.0 and 1.1 shall be disabled. Target: TLS >= 1.2 on all connections.' HOP BY HOP, MEASURED. (1) APPLICATION TO SQL SERVER - SATISFIED ON ENCRYPTION, UNPINNED ON VERSION. The connection string carries Encrypt=True, so the channel is encrypted; it also carries TrustServerCertificate=True, which the compose file's own comment describes accurately as encrypted but NOT authenticated - it stops passive sniffing, not an active man in the middle, and moving to a CA-issued certificate is documented as the operator's step. No TLS version floor is configured on this hop by ACMP; 1.2-or-higher is whatever SQL Server 2022 and the .NET driver negotiate. (2) APPLICATION TO TARSEEM SIDECAR - THE SURFACE DOES NOT EXIST. Tarseem is Phase 2 and P14 was deferred INDEFINITELY by DEC-028; a repository-wide search for the name across C# and TypeScript returns exactly one hit, PlaceholderPage.tsx. A hop with no endpoint cannot carry TLS, and this is the one clause that can honestly be excluded BY NAME. (3) APPLICATION TO KEYCLOAK - PLAINTEXT ON THE INTERNAL NETWORK, IN EVERY ENVIRONMENT. deploy/nginx/cloud-443.conf.template line 121 is proxy_pass http://keycloak:8080/ and line 145 is proxy_pass http://api:8080; deploy/nginx/default.conf.template line 58 does the same for dev. KeycloakAdmin__BaseUrl defaults to http://keycloak:8080/ in BOTH compose files. So every hop behind the reverse proxy is unencrypted HTTP over the Docker network. THE ONE PLACE TLS IS CONFIGURED IS THE PUBLIC EDGE, AND IT IS CONFIGURED WELL: cloud-443.conf.template line 30 sets ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3, which is exactly the floor NFR-019 states, with certificates published by certbot-deploy-hook.sh. WHY THIS IS A DEFECT ROW RATHER THAN A DEFERRED-WORK ROW: nothing here is unbuilt or half-built. The deployment does what it was designed to do, and OQ-024 shows the design was deliberate - its resolution reads 'TLS 1.2+ on the public endpoint (1.3 preferred if all clients support it); no mTLS in v1 for internal Compose-network services'. That resolution answers a DIFFERENT question than NFR-019 asks: it settles the public edge and it settles mTLS, and it is silent on whether internal hops need ordinary TLS. So the register contains a requirement mandating TLS on internal hops and a resolved open question describing an internal network that deliberately has none, and NOTHING RECONCILES THEM. Same class as DEF-098, where NFR-027 mandated MinIO after a ratified ADR had replaced it. THE DISPOSITION IS THE OPERATOR'S and the two directions are genuinely different: narrow NFR-019 to the trust boundary it evidently meant - the public endpoint plus the database hop - naming the internal Docker network as an accepted boundary the way OQ-024 already does for mTLS; or treat internal plaintext as a real gap and keep the requirement as the target. NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: the version floor is unpinned on every hop except the public edge, so even the narrowed version would inherit DW-073's shape.

title:
NFR-013 IS A MUST-PRIORITY REQUIREMENT MANDATING A STORAGE MECHANISM THAT A RATIFIED ADR DELETED, AND THREE FURTHER RECORDS STILL ASSERT THE DELETED MECHANISM. Operator disposition 2026-08-20: RECORD THE CONFLICT, CHANGE NOTHING - NFR-013 keeps its text, consistent with the register being kept as a statement of the target rather than of the status quo, the same call made for the minimal-base clause and for internal transport encryption.

WHAT THE REQUIREMENT SAYS. NFR-013, priority Must, status Approved: 'The SQL Server database shall support columnstore-indexed reporting queries (dashboard aggregations) over 3 years of data (estimated 10 000-50 000 rows across governed entities) with result times under 3 seconds. Target: Dashboard query P95 under 3 000 ms with 50 000-row dataset.' It names columnstore indexing as the mechanism, not merely the latency as the outcome.

WHAT THE ARCHITECTURE DECIDED INSTEAD. ADR-0022, Approved, titled 'Reporting is client-side aggregation over thin registers - no columnstore read-model layer, no chart library'. Its first decision clause reads: 'No Reporting read-model tables, no columnstore, no /api/v1/reports/* aggregation endpoints in v1. Dashboards and reports are composed in the SPA from the modules' own public register reads.' Its context is explicit that the read-model layer specified in the reporting domain document is disproportionate for a single committee, on-prem, 20 users or fewer, with registers holding a few hundred rows.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. Verified 2026-08-20 rather than assumed. A search for columnstore across all migrations and all of src returns no index definition anywhere; the only source hits are two comments that state its ABSENCE. src/Acmp.Web/src/features/dashboard/dashboardAgg.ts line 4 reads 'columnstore (ADR-0022, right-sized for under 20 users)' as part of a sentence describing what the module does NOT use, and src/Acmp.Web/src/features/reports/reportViews.ts line 6 says 'read-model, no columnstore, no chart library - CSS primitives'. So the code agrees with the ADR and disagrees with the requirement, and it says so in its own comments.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS BIGGER THAN TWO ROWS. A keyword sweep of the decision, ADR and open-question registers - not an identifier sweep, which would have found nothing, since neither NFR-013 nor ADR-0022 contains the other's identifier - surfaced three more records that still assert the deleted mechanism. DEC-020, Approved: 'Primary datastore - Microsoft SQL Server only (transactional + columnstore reporting + FTS); no second database.' ADR-0003, Approved, 'Microsoft SQL Server as the Single Datastore', which carries the same reasoning. And OQ-040, which asks which SQL Server edition runs the bundled production instance - a question whose answer bears directly on this, because columnstore indexing is not available on every edition. So the register holds one Approved ADR removing columnstore and three Approved records still treating it as part of why SQL Server was chosen at all. ADR-0022 says it EXTENDS ADR-0003 rather than superseding it, which is why nothing was flagged.

WHY NO GATE OR RULE SEES IT. This is not a foreign key, an edge, or a status. It is a technology named in the prose of one record and unnamed-but-negated in the prose of another. G-IDS checks foreign keys and entity-index consistency; G-TRACE checks that requirements have links, not that the links agree. The only instrument that finds it is a human or an agent sweeping by KEYWORD, which is the practice the eighth lesson records, and this is the fourth time that lesson has fired on this project - the previous instance being a storage-technology requirement that a later ADR replaced by name.

SEVERITY. Medium. Nothing in the product is broken and no dashboard is slow; the requirement's own latency target may well be met by the client-side composition, which nobody has measured because that measurement needs a running stack and a seeded dataset. What is wrong is that a Must requirement specifies an implementation the architecture deliberately rejected, so any future reader reconciling the two will either build a columnstore layer that ADR-0022 forbids or quietly reword the requirement to match what shipped, which is the direction DEF-088 records as never-silent.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT, none of which is done here. Either a scope change narrowing NFR-013 to its latency target and dropping the named mechanism, which the operator declined today as the easy path; or a new decision recording that ADR-0022 amends DEC-020 and ADR-0003 on this point, which would at least make the four records consistent with each other while leaving NFR-013 as the unmet target; or answering OQ-040, since an edition without columnstore support would make the requirement unsatisfiable by construction rather than merely unimplemented. The deferred-work row covering NFR-013's latency measurement stays open and unchanged - its timing half still needs a running stack, and this defect covers only the mechanism half its own text told a later session to check.

title: THE KANBAN VIEW SHOWS ONLY THE FIRST 25 TOPICS OF A COLUMN AND OFFERS NO WAY TO REACH THE REST. Found 2026-08-21 while building DW-040's drag-to-reprioritize, which is what makes it matter more than it did yesterday. THE MECHANISM, verified rather than inferred: Backlog.tsx declares PAGE_SIZE = 25 and sends pageSize on EVERY request including the kanban's, but the pager is rendered inside a `view !== 'kanban'` guard, and setPage is wired to nothing else - no infinite scroll, no load-more, no per-column fetch. So the kanban receives a PREFIX of the filtered result and there is no control anywhere on the surface that advances it. THE USER IS TOLD AND CANNOT ACT: the 'showing X of Y' count in the filter bar IS rendered in kanban view, so a Secretary looking at 60 triage topics reads 'showing 25 of 60' beside a board that will never display the other 35. That is arguably worse than silent truncation, because the interface states the problem and withholds the remedy. WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC: the kanban is the PRIORITIZATION surface. FR-037's drag and FR-034's keyboard reorder both act on it. A topic sitting at position 26 could not be dragged, moved up, or seen - unreachable for the exact operation the screen exists to perform - while MoveTopicPriority materializes the WHOLE column server-side and renumbers it 1..N, so reordering the visible 25 silently renumbered the invisible 35 too. FIXED 2026-08-21 by PR #303 (squashed to f323240). THE FIX ADDRESSES REACH, NOT DISCLOSURE, because disclosure already existed and was useless on its own: the kanban now requests a bounded KANBAN_PAGE_SIZE of 500 instead of 25, and when the result is STILL truncated the board says so and tells the user to narrow the filters. Per-column pagination and lazy loading were rejected for reintroducing the same defect one column at a time - the board needs the WHOLE column because priority order is relative. Unbounded was rejected because GetBacklog applies no upper cap to pageSize, so an uncapped request is a request-size hazard; that separate finding is filed under its own row. 500 covers this deployment's realistic scale: CON-001 caps it at 20 users and the backlog read already excludes Closed, Converted and Rejected, so the budget spans active plus Decided topics only. THE RESIDUAL IS NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: 500 is a ceiling, not a guarantee, and the notice is what makes the beyond-ceiling case honest.
